findings.title: Snippet-only corpus inflates retrieval metrics
findings.detail: The retrieval-eval corpus is built entirely from the eval questions' own gold snippets with zero distractors (default-OFF), so coverage@>=1 = 1.0 and the 'retrieval effectiveness' view is numerically identical to the 'end-to-end' view. Ranking metrics (MRR 0.961, nDCG@5 0.833) are optimistic and the two-view distinction collapses. This is a disclosed design choice, not a hidden coverage gap; the report states the 83.96% distinct-PMID ceiling and the 62 partially-covered queries.

findings.title: Advertised coverage flags are inert
findings.detail: --add-training-distractors only warns if the file is missing and --fetch-missing prints 'not auto-enabled'; neither actually ingests or fetches. The evaluation report describes them as flags that 'exist (default OFF) to raise coverage', which overstates them. Both are out of gated scope; report wording should match behavior.

findings.title: Artifact filenames differ from the review brief
findings.detail: The gate prompt referenced diagnostics.json, retrieval_metrics.json, calibration_metrics.json at the top level; the real files live under diagnostics/, retrieval/, and calibration/. All content is present and consistent with the gate requirements; only the paths differ.
